clue.text: One comes from among relatively unrefined types

definitions.text: One comes from among relatively unrefined types

indicators.note: something that comes from a run of words is drawn out of their letters, so the answer sits inside these two words

explanation.surface: Someone of humble stock emerges from a fairly coarse crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'among relatively', and the whole clue doubles as a description: a mongrel is a dog of mixed, unpedigreed breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog of mixed, unpedigreed breed descends from parents of no refined lineage.

clue.text: 1,001 brushed aside by Cromwell

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, the 1,000 part
an ace is a one in cards or dice, supplying the final 1

explanation.surface: A precise number is dismissed by the Lord Protector.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 1,001 as 1,000 plus 1: M then ACE. Cromwell, dissolving the Rump Parliament in 1653, ordered its ceremonial mace removed as 'that bauble'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial staff of the Commons was the object Oliver Cromwell famously dismissed as a bauble.

clue.text: Organised stock

explanation.definitionFit: Tidy and orderly both describe it; separately it is an archaic term for oxen or cattle.

clue.text: Troop cover after engineers cut expenses

indicators.note: after places the troops' cover behind the engineers in the answer

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
soldiers take cover in a trench

explanation.surface: Soldiers dig in behind the sappers while the budget is slashed.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise or reduce spending is to cut back, a standard synonym.

clue.text: Playing lute softly to relieve tension

indicators.note: playing the word lute treats its letters loosely, rearranging them

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for softly

explanation.surface: A gentle lute performance helps someone unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off or slacken is to stop pressing, an everyday phrasal verb.

clue.text: Ford is hesitating to become emperor

parts.note: the Ka is a small Ford car model
taken as written
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A dithering Ford is crowned as a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford' looks like a person (Henry or Harrison) but names the car maker's small Ka model.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the title of the German and Austrian emperors, from the Latin Caesar.

clue.text: Fruit, not originally but still …

indicators.note: not originally tells us to drop the opening letter of the fruit word

parts.note: bananas are a fruit

explanation.surface: A fruit that loses its first letter is nonetheless still a fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Behead BANANAS and what remains is still a fruit: the French and botanical name for the pineapple.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the pineapple's name in French and many other languages, so a fruit even after losing its B.

clue.text: Dubious, like the filth?

definitions.meaning: the filth is British slang for the police, who are by trade mistrustful

explanation.definitionFit: Questionable things arouse mistrust; police officers, the filth in British slang, are mistrustful by habit.

clue.text: Arbitrator in mad dance borrowed from Peter to pay Paul

definitions.text: borrowed from Peter to pay Paul

parts.note: a referee, REF, arbitrates in sport
taken as written

indicators.note: a mad dance is a wild one, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A referee gets carried away in a frenzied dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arbitrator' suggests a judge or mediator, but here the sporting official; 'mad' is the anagram signal on the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking out a new loan to pay off an old one is robbing Peter to pay Paul.

clue.text: Virtue of endless hurry in financial centre

indicators.note: in places the shortened hurry inside the financial centre

parts.note: the City is London's financial district

indicators.note: endless says the last letter of the hurry word goes

parts.note: haste means hurry

explanation.surface: Purity is hard to find amid the rush of the City.
explanation.walkthrough: London's financial district is simply called the City, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexual abstinence or purity is traditionally counted among the virtues.

clue.text: High Church service provided it's in central France

parts.note: a High Mass is a Church service with full ceremony
if means provided that

explanation.surface: An Anglo-Catholic ceremony is offered on condition it takes place in the heart of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' looks like the definition (an upland) but belongs with Church service: High Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: The Massif Central is the great upland region in the middle of France.

clue.text: Listen to variation of New Testament date

indicators.note: a variation of something is a reworking of it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Heed a revised dating of the Gospels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variation of' rearranges NT and DATE together.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay heed or give ear is to listen, an older sense of the verb.

clue.text: Commission for distribution of dog food

parts.note: per means for, as in per head
a pet ration is a share of food dealt out to the dog

explanation.surface: A fee is charged for handing out dog food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commission' looks like a payment but is the act of committing, as in the commission of a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Committing a crime is its commission, the carrying out of a deed.

clue.text: "It can be done — somehow I have" (Cable)

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters get there in some loose order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Vince Cable insists he has somehow managed it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges I HAVE and CABLE together; Cable recalls the Lib Dem minister quoted at the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Something possible or attainable is one that can be done.

clue.text: Bacon's original source

parts.note: bacon starts life as a young pig, so its first source is the piglet still at the sow

explanation.surface: Where Francis Bacon got his ideas from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bacon' looks like the philosopher or painter, but means the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A young piglet still feeding from its mother is where pork and bacon begin.

clue.text: A pious type, Winston, fit to move the queen

indicators.note: fit means not ill, so the ill is taken from Winston's surname

parts.note: Winston Churchill, wartime British prime minister
go means move
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen

explanation.surface: Churchill is well enough to shift the queen, a devout figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' leaves CHURCHILL without ILL, giving CHURCH; 'fit' looks like 'able' but means 'not ill'.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular attender at services is a devout or pious person.

clue.text: Attic half overturned, brought to order

indicators.note: half overturned turns only the second half of the attic word back to front

parts.note: a garret is an attic room

explanation.surface: Half the loft is turned upside down and tidied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half overturned' reverses RET at the end of GARRET to TER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garter is the senior English order of chivalry, founded by Edward III.

clue.text: In name it may be called the King's Arms

definitions.text: it may be called the King's Arms

parts.note: taken as written; the run across In name is a coincidence of the charade, not a hiding
N is an abbreviation for name; its sitting beside In is a coincidence, not a hidden word

explanation.surface: Something could take the name King's Arms.
explanation.walkthrough: The King's Arms is a common British pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubs and taverns often bear names like the King's Arms.

clue.text: Stern — apt perhaps to take one side or the other

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters might be arranged otherwise

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A severe person is likely to pick sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges STERN and APT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Each arm of a cross-shaped church, either side of the nave, is this part.

clue.text: Liquid, one not known to be undrinkable

definitions.text: Liquid, one not known to be undrinkable

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one; that the letters also sit inside undrinkable is a coincidence of the surface
NK abbreviates not known

explanation.surface: A fluid of uncertain safety is not to be drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing fluid is a coloured liquid used in pens and printing, and nobody would drink it.

clue.text: The way stuff comes and goes

definitions.text: The way stuff comes and goes

parts.words: The way stuff comes and goes
parts.note: the way here is a literal route along which goods travel to and from markets

explanation.surface: Things come and go in the way of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' looks like a manner, but it is a path; 'stuff' is merchandise.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial path used by merchants carries goods in both directions.

clue.text: Cope with a boy when grown up?

definitions.meaning: split as ..., the time of life when a boy has become a man

explanation.definitionFit: To handle or deal with is a standard synonym; split as man age it is a boy's adulthood.

clue.text: With vehicle, possibly, get in a top position

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Grab a van, if you can, to reach the highest spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top position' reads as the definition, but 'top' is anagram fodder and only 'position' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A viewpoint or advantageous position, such as a good spot for observing.

clue.text: It may be high, but it's nothing grim

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
dour means grim or stern

explanation.surface: It may be lofty but there is nothing gloomy in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' here means strong-smelling, as with high game.
explanation.definitionFit: A smell can be high, meaning strong or tainted, as with game kept too long.

clue.text: Smith, a bit short of specialist food provider

indicators.note: a bit short says the cook's name loses a little, its last letter

parts.note: Delia Smith is a famous British TV cook

explanation.surface: A cookery writer falls slightly short of running a speciality shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Delia Smith is Britain's best-known TV cookery writer; dropping her final A leaves DELI.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen sells speciality foods such as cured meats and cheeses.

clue.text: A good deal of land seen as one article

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Much property is regarded as a single item.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the largest continent, so a very great deal of land indeed.

clue.text: Backstage chatter, or how Miller unmasked McCarthy?

definitions.meaning: side action or talk going on apart from the main scene
Arthur Miller attacked McCarthyism by means of a play, The Crucible

explanation.definitionFit: Subsidiary action going on aside from the main business, especially on stage.

clue.text: Increasingly out and about, as are the rich when partying

definitions.text: Increasingly out and about, as are the rich when partying

parts.words: Increasingly out and about, as are the rich when partying
parts.note: split as ..., being away from home ever more, as socialites are; also those sleeping rough

explanation.surface: The wealthy spend more and more of their time out on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken whole it means those without a place to live; split, it is 'less at home', like party-going rich folk.
explanation.definitionFit: People sleeping rough have nowhere to live and are always out in the street.

clue.text: Bird could be elegant, apart from name

indicators.note: could be hints that the letters may be rearranged
apart from says a letter is set aside from the rearranged letters

explanation.surface: A bird might look graceful, except for what it is called.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N out of ELEGANT and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A young eagle is a bird, specifically an eagle's chick.

clue.text: Drink needs part of the eye keeping direction

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the direction sits within the eye part

parts.note: the retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye
S is south, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A drink requires an eye that holds its bearings.
explanation.definitionFit: This resin-flavoured Greek white wine is an alcoholic drink.
